core.convergence@1.0.0.caption_plain: 4 of 6 parameters have not converged (R-hat more than 1.01 or fewer than 200 effective samples), for example beta[tv], alpha[east], sigma. Before you trust the results, run the sampler longer, increase the tuning or reparameterise the model. There were 3 divergent transitions. The estimates can be biased.
core.convergence@1.0.0.title: Sampler convergence

core.counterfactual@1.0.0.caption_plain: The scenario changes total revenue by 184 (90% interval 139 to 251) compared with the baseline. Probability of an increase: 100%.
core.counterfactual@1.0.0.title: Scenario vs baseline

core.data_overview@1.0.0.caption_plain: Each panel shows one variable over week, with one line for each geo. The values show the sum over channel. spend has the most missing values (3% overall). The groups (geo) have from 19 to 20 observed values of revenue.
core.data_overview@1.0.0.title: Data overview

core.decision_distribution@1.0.0.caption_plain: shift_tv is the best option with probability 50%. Its expected objective is 0.92 (90% interval -0.56 to 2.58).
core.decision_distribution@1.0.0.title: Decision outcome

core.decomposition@1.0.0.caption_plain: For the full period, the outcome divides into: baseline 94%, tv 5%, search 2%. The values show the sum over geo.
core.decomposition@1.0.0.title: Decomposition

core.fit_vs_actual@1.0.0.caption_plain: Each dot compares an actual value of revenue with the prediction of the model. Dots on the dashed line are perfect predictions. The model explains 52% of the variation (R² = 0.52) with a typical error of 4% (MAPE).
core.fit_vs_actual@1.0.0.title: Predicted vs actual

core.model_comparison@1.0.0.caption_plain: unbiased has the best expected predictive accuracy (waic). biased is 32.3 ± 0.0 elpd worse: a clear difference. WAIC comes from the stored log-likelihood. Use PSIS-LOO when it is available.
core.model_comparison@1.0.0.title: Model comparison

core.posterior_forest@1.0.0.caption_plain: Each row is a model parameter. The dot is the posterior median. The thick bar is the central 50% interval. The thin line is the 94% highest-density interval. 6 of 6 intervals do not include zero.
core.posterior_forest@1.0.0.title: Posterior forest

core.ppc@1.0.0.caption_plain: 100% of the observations of revenue are in the 90% predictive interval of the model (ideal: about 90%). Very few observations are in the tails. The intervals are possibly too wide.
core.ppc@1.0.0.title: Posterior predictive check

core.ppc_fan@1.0.0.caption_plain: The line is the median estimate of revenue from the model. The shaded bands are the 50% and 90% intervals. The dots are the actual values. The dashed line marks where the training data ends.
core.ppc_fan@1.0.0.title: Fit and forecast

core.prior_predictive@1.0.0.caption_plain: The grey curves are datasets of revenue that the model can make before it sees data. The black curve is your data. Your data should look similar to the grey curves. 100% of the observations are in the prior 90% range.

vconcat.title: Prior predictive revenue over week (mean over geo)

core.prior_predictive@1.0.0.title: Prior predictive check

core.residuals_over_time@1.0.0.caption_plain: Residuals are actual minus predicted revenue. They should stay near zero. There is no important average bias.
core.residuals_over_time@1.0.0.title: Residuals over time

ml.feature_importance@1.0.0.caption_plain: The plot shows all 5 features. The model uses price most. It has 42% of the total importance. Importances show what the model uses. They do not show cause and effect.
ml.feature_importance@1.0.0.title: Feature importance

mmm.budget_plans@1.0.0.caption_plain: plan_b is expected to deliver 26.2 (3%) more outcome than current (90% interval -15.9 to 66.6). The probability that it is better: 84%.
mmm.budget_plans@1.0.0.title: Budget plan comparison

mmm.decomposition@1.0.0.caption_plain: For the full period, the outcome divides into: baseline 94%, tv 5%, search 2%. The values show the sum over geo.
mmm.decomposition@1.0.0.title: Contribution by component

mmm.marginal_cost@1.0.0.caption_plain: The cost per extra unit of response at each spend level in each channel. The shaded area is the 90% interval. At current spend, the cheapest next unit comes from tv (2.26).
mmm.marginal_cost@1.0.0.title: Marginal cost

mmm.prior_beliefs@1.0.0.caption_plain: Before the model sees the KPI, it puts the value of each channel on the black line (90% of the prior) and mostly in the dark bar (50%). The tick is at the median. The light band is the range that you gave. tv: 88% of the prior is in your range (you said 80%); search: 94% of the prior is in your range (you said 90%); baseline: 94% of the prior is in your range (you said 80%).
mmm.prior_beliefs@1.0.0.title: Your beliefs and the priors

mmm.response_curves@1.0.0.caption_plain: Each curve shows the expected response for each level of spend in a channel. The shaded area is the 90% interval. A steeper curve returns more for each extra unit of spend. A curve that becomes flat shows that the channel is near saturation. At current spend (diamonds), tv is closest to saturation. An extra unit there returns 29% of the return at its steepest point.
mmm.response_curves@1.0.0.title: Response curves

sci.ensemble@1.0.0.caption_plain: The thin lines are 40 draws from the model. Each line is one possible path of y along time. The shaded band is the 90% interval of all 60 draws. The thick line is the median. The dots are the actual values. 96% of the actual values are in the 90% band.
sci.ensemble@1.0.0.title: Ensemble of y

sci.field_map@1.0.0.caption_plain: Each panel shows one statistic of intensity for each cell, from 80 draws of the posterior. The mean panel shows the average value. The sd panel shows the uncertainty. A high sd shows where the data do not fix the value. Empty cells have no value.
sci.field_map@1.0.0.title: Field map of intensity

sci.profile_bands@1.0.0.caption_plain: Each line is the median of u along x for one t. Use the slider to show one t with its bands. The bands are the 50% and 90% intervals. The dots are the actual values. 95% of the actual values are in the 90% band.
sci.profile_bands@1.0.0.title: Profiles of u

sci.vector_field@1.0.0.caption_plain: The colours show the length of the traction vector in each cell, from 60 draws of the model. The arrows on the mean panel show the mean direction. A longer arrow shows a larger mean vector. The sd panel shows where the data do not fix the length of the vector.
sci.vector_field@1.0.0.title: Vector field of traction
